content.overview: An intervention is not complete when it is applied or released; it is complete when its effect is measured, incompatibilities and adverse effects are assessed, records are reconstructable and the next decision follows the evidence.

vocabulary.definition: Planned follow-up measurement used to determine whether an intervention produced the intended result.
Review of whether one intervention could reduce the effectiveness or safety of another tactic, organism, process or crop condition.
Evaluation of why a pest/pathogen problem returned and whether prevention, detection, intervention or verification controls need revision.

sections.title: Use comparable monitoring before and after
sections.body: Post-intervention counts or severity observations are only comparable when route, timing, sampled units and method are compatible. A lower count from a smaller sample is not evidence of improvement.

sections.title: Track unintended effects and compatibility
sections.body: Review crop stress, beneficial-organism survival, environmental changes and new hotspots as part of the response. A tactic that suppresses the target but disrupts the larger IPM system may need revision.

sections.title: Preserve the decision trail
sections.body: Records should show original evidence, intervention, authorization, monitoring method, result, deviations and follow-up. Corrections should preserve rather than overwrite the original history.

workedExamples: A pest count falls after treatment, but the follow-up sample covered only one previously clean bench. The result cannot support room-wide closure.
commonMistakes: Closing an IPM event immediately after intervention.
Changing sampling methods without documenting the change.
Recording only successful outcomes and losing evidence about failures or recurrence.
content.practicalApplication: Build an intervention verification record with baseline, tactic, authorization, compatibility check, follow-up schedule, comparable metric, failure trigger and closure criteria.
content.summary: IPM improves when every intervention produces usable evidence. Comparable verification and reconstructable records turn control actions into program learning.
